social.title: Catch No-Cover Live Music at Pengilly's Saloon
social.description: A 140-capacity Old Boise saloon that Esquire once put on its top-100 bars list, with live music most nights and usually no cover.
social.bonus: Stay through a full set by a band you have never heard of.

social.title: Go to an Idaho Steelheads Game
social.description: Minor league hockey downtown at Idaho Central Arena, loud and fast and cheap, with a crowd that takes it seriously.
social.bonus: Learn one Steelheads chant and actually use it.

social.title: Drink Idaho Beer at Bittercreek Alehouse
social.description: The 8th Street beer bar that made Boise care about draft lists, open late with a kitchen that sources as hard as the taps do.
social.bonus: Order a beer from a brewery nobody at your table has heard of.

social.title: Catch a Drag Night at The Balcony Club
social.description: Boise's queer nightclub on the Grove, running drag, burlesque, aerial and queer-oke five nights a week from a second-floor balcony over 8th Street.
social.bonus: Tip a performer in person instead of from your seat.

social.title: Drink a Proper Cocktail at Press & Pony
social.description: A small 1920s-styled bar on Idaho Street making its own tonics and sodas, where the bartenders would rather ask what you like than hand you a list.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender three flavours you like and drink whatever appears.

social.title: Walk the Garden City Ale Trail
social.description: Barbarian Brewing's barrel-aged sours and Western Collective's rotating taproom sit within walking distance of each other off Chinden.
social.bonus: Order the sourest thing on each list and finish both.

social.title: Take the Rooftop at 10 Barrel Brewing
social.description: A Bannock Street brewpub whose rooftop patio is the easiest golden-hour seat in downtown Boise.
social.bonus: Get up there before sunset and hold the table until dark.

social.title: Catch a Show at the Knitting Factory
social.description: A thousand-capacity concert house on 9th Street that pulls national touring acts through a city this size all year.
social.bonus: Get to the barrier for the opener, not just the headliner.

social.title: Watch the Boise Hawks at Memorial Stadium
social.description: A 3,500-seat ballpark on the bank of the Boise River where cheap summer baseball comes with a mountain backdrop.
social.bonus: Sit on the grass berm instead of a seat and catch a foul ball.

social.title: Do Treefort Music Fest Across Downtown
social.description: Five days every spring when every venue, alley and parking lot downtown becomes a stage for hundreds of bands nobody has heard of yet.
social.bonus: See five acts in one day that you had never heard of that morning.

social.title: See a Game on the Blue Turf at Albertsons Stadium
social.description: The most recognisable field in college football is bright blue, and a Boise State Saturday is the loudest thing that happens in Idaho.
social.bonus: Wear blue and orange and stay for the entire fourth quarter.

social.title: See a Touring Band at Neurolux
social.description: The Hitchcock Building lounge that has been Boise's indie rock room for decades, open 365 days a year with a photo booth in the corner.
social.bonus: Get in the photo booth before the headliner starts.

8ball.title: The Greenbelt Coin Flip
8ball.description: Start anywhere on the Greenbelt, flip a coin at every fork and bridge, and ride until you are somewhere you have never been.
8ball.bonus: When you run out of path, find the nearest patio and stay for one drink.

8ball.title: Basque Block Roulette
8ball.description: Three doors on one short block on Grove Street: hit all of them and order the first item on each menu you cannot pronounce.
8ball.bonus: Do not look anything up until after you have eaten it.

culture.title: Read the Walls at the Anne Frank Memorial
culture.description: The only human rights memorial of its kind in the United States, an open-air amphitheatre on the Greenbelt engraved with sixty quotes and the full Declaration of Human Rights.
culture.bonus: Read one quote out loud to the person you came with.

culture.title: Climb the Dome at the Idaho State Capitol
culture.description: The only geothermally heated state capitol in America, free to walk into, with four floors of sandstone and marble under a glass-floored rotunda.
culture.bonus: Get to the top floor and look straight down through the rotunda floor.

culture.title: Tour the Old Idaho Penitentiary
culture.description: A territorial prison that held inmates from 1872 to 1973 and is now open cell by cell, including solitary and the gallows room.
culture.bonus: Stand alone inside a solitary cell with the door shut for a full minute.

culture.title: Spend an Afternoon in the Boise Art Museum
culture.description: Idaho's only accredited art museum, on the edge of Julia Davis Park, strong on contemporary Northwest work and ceramics.
culture.bonus: Pick the single piece you would steal and explain why to whoever you came with.

culture.title: See Anything at All Inside the Egyptian Theatre
culture.description: A 1927 Egyptian Revival movie palace on Main Street, still the oldest theatre in the city and still running films, tribute shows and sing-alongs under its painted ceiling.
culture.bonus: Sit in the balcony and look up before the lights go down.

culture.title: Walk Freak Alley Gallery
culture.description: An entire downtown alley off 8th Street given over to murals and repainted every year, the largest outdoor gallery in the Northwest.
culture.bonus: Find the piece you would put on your wall and photograph only that one.

culture.title: Visit the Basque Museum & Cultural Center
culture.description: Boise holds one of the largest Basque populations outside Europe, and this Grove Street museum includes the 1864 boarding house that housed the first arrivals.
culture.bonus: Learn to say one full sentence in Euskara before you leave.

culture.title: Visit the Idaho Black History Museum
culture.description: Housed in a relocated 1921 church in Julia Davis Park, telling a part of Idaho's story that almost nothing else in the state covers.
culture.bonus: Ask the person at the desk what most visitors get wrong about Idaho.

chill.title: Stroll 13th Street Through Hyde Park
chill.description: The North End's four-block historic village of cafes, pubs and shops under a heavy tree canopy, best walked with no plan at all.
chill.bonus: Walk the whole strip once before deciding where to stop.

chill.title: Take a Slow Morning at Neckar Coffee
chill.description: A Boise roaster with a bright 10th Street cafe that takes its filter coffee seriously enough to tell you the farm.
chill.bonus: Order a pour-over and sit without opening your phone once.

chill.title: Claim a Fire Pit at Payette Brewing's Beer Garden
chill.description: An 11,000-square-foot riverside beer garden off River Street with a ten-foot fire pit, a bocce court, yard games and a stage for local bands.
chill.bonus: Win a bocce match against someone you just met.

chill.title: Lose an Hour in Rediscovered Books
chill.description: Boise's independent bookshop, now in a bigger Linen District space on West Grove with its own event room and staff picks worth trusting.
chill.bonus: Buy the book a bookseller recommends, not the one you came in for.

chill.title: Dig Through the Bins at The Record Exchange
chill.description: Idaho's largest independent record store, open daily on West Idaho Street with an espresso bar in the front and deep used vinyl in the back.
chill.bonus: Buy a record purely because of its cover.

chill.title: Walk the Loop at Kathryn Albertson Park
chill.description: Forty-one acres of ponds, reeds and gazebos kept deliberately quiet as a wildlife refuge, minutes from downtown.
chill.bonus: Spot a great blue heron before you finish the loop.

chill.title: Catch Something Foreign at The Flicks
chill.description: Four screens of independent and foreign film since 1984, with a cafe and a patio where you can take a glass of wine into the theatre.
chill.bonus: Buy a ticket for whatever starts next without reading the synopsis.

chill.title: Picnic by the Fountain at Ann Morrison Park
chill.description: 153 riverside acres with a huge central fountain, open lawns and enough space that you can always find an empty corner.
chill.bonus: Bring one thing to share that you made yourself.

chill.title: Taste Idaho Wine on the River at Telaya
chill.description: A Garden City winery right on the Greenbelt with a dog-friendly deck, above-ground fire pits and a food truck most days.
chill.bonus: Order the full flight and pick your favourite before the pourer tells you the prices.

chill.title: Wander the Idaho Botanical Garden
chill.description: Fifteen acres of themed gardens on the old penitentiary grounds, backed right up against the foothills.
chill.bonus: Find the quietest bench in the garden and sit on it for ten full minutes.

foodie.title: Order the Handmade Pasta at Alavita
foodie.description: An Italian joint in the old City National Bank building at 8th and Idaho, rolling every pasta in house with Northwest flour and local eggs.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar and let the bartender pick the wine by the glass.

foodie.title: Order Finger Steaks at Westside Drive In
foodie.description: Chef Lou's 1957 drive-in serves the buttermilk-battered finger steaks that are Idaho's actual state dish, with cocktail sauce and a side of fry sauce.
foodie.bonus: Order the ice cream potato for dessert and finish the whole thing.

foodie.title: Graze Saturday at the Capital City Public Market
foodie.description: Every Saturday morning from April to December, Main Street closes and fills with Idaho growers, makers and breakfast stalls.
foodie.bonus: Buy lunch entirely from three different stalls and eat it on a curb.

foodie.title: Wait for a Table at Goldy's Breakfast Bistro
foodie.description: Boise's breakfast institution on Capitol Boulevard, where the line out the door on a Saturday is part of the experience.
foodie.bonus: Build the whole plate from the sides menu instead of ordering an entree.

foodie.title: Order a Scoop Flight at The STIL
foodie.description: Short for The Sweetest Things In Life, a Boise ice cream shop that will pair scoops with local beer or wine if you ask.
foodie.bonus: Get the boozy flight and guess which scoop has the alcohol in it.

foodie.title: Pick a Weird One at Guru Donuts
foodie.description: Ground floor of the historic Idanha Building, turning out scratch-made raised, cake and vegan donuts with glazes that change constantly.
foodie.bonus: Order the strangest flavour on the board without asking what is in it.

foodie.title: Drink Spirits Made Onsite at Bardenay
foodie.description: On the Basque Block, the first restaurant distillery ever licensed in America, distilling its own gin, vodka and rum behind the bar since 1999.
foodie.bonus: Order a cocktail built only from spirits distilled in the building.

foodie.title: Drink a Saffron Latte at Sunshine Spice Cafe
foodie.description: Boise's first Afghan cafe, opened by the Shams sisters, where the saffron, cardamom and pistachio lattes come with pastries baked that morning.
foodie.bonus: Order something off the pastry case you cannot pronounce.

foodie.title: Catch Paella Day at The Basque Market
foodie.description: On the Basque Block they cook a giant pan of paella outdoors on Wednesdays and Fridays at noon and serve it on the patio until it runs out.
foodie.bonus: Get there before the pan is half gone and eat standing up with strangers.

foodie.title: Eat Local Everything at Fork
foodie.description: The 8th Street corner restaurant that built its whole menu on Northwest producers, and still the easiest good dinner in downtown Boise.
foodie.bonus: Ask your server which farm the main ingredient came from before you order.

foodie.title: Build a Fry Flight at Boise Fry Company
foodie.description: A restaurant that treats the burger as a side dish, with six potato varieties, six cuts and a wall of house dipping sauces.
foodie.bonus: Order three potato types and rank them out loud before you leave.

foodie.title: Book the Tasting Menu at KIN
foodie.description: Kris Komori became the first Idaho chef to win a James Beard Award here, cooking a multicourse Idaho menu at a communal table that changes every month.
foodie.bonus: Take the wine pairing and let them choose every glass.

adventure.title: Surf the Standing Wave at Boise Whitewater Park
adventure.description: An engineered river wave in the middle of a landlocked city, where locals line up with surfboards and kayaks on summer evenings.
adventure.bonus: Take one ride, however short, instead of only watching from the bank.

adventure.title: Hike the Foothills to Stack Rock
adventure.description: A quiet climb through ponderosa above Bogus Basin Road to a granite outcrop that scramblers and climbers have to themselves most mornings.
adventure.bonus: Get to the base of the rock and touch the summit block.

adventure.title: Take Night Laps Under the Lights at Bogus Basin
adventure.description: Boise's nonprofit mountain lights 165 acres after dark, so you can leave work at five and be carving empty runs by six-thirty.
adventure.bonus: Ski the last chair of the night, then drive down with the windows open.

adventure.title: Sandboard the Dunes and Stargaze at Bruneau
adventure.description: North America's tallest single-structure sand dune is an hour south of Boise, and the park's public observatory opens its telescopes once the sky goes black.
adventure.bonus: Ride the big dune down on a board, then stay for the last telescope of the night.

adventure.title: Hike Table Rock for Sunset Over the Valley
adventure.description: A steady climb up the sandstone bluff east of downtown puts the whole Treasure Valley under a pink sky with the lit cross at your back.
adventure.bonus: Time it so you reach the top the moment the streetlights come on.

adventure.title: Swim at Sandy Point Beach Below Lucky Peak
adventure.description: A calm, sandy swimming cove at the foot of Lucky Peak Dam where the cold reservoir water and a hundred-foot fountain do the work on a hot afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Swim all the way out to the fountain spray.

adventure.title: Ride the Glade Runner Mountain Coaster
adventure.description: Bogus Basin's gravity coaster pulls you 800 vertical feet up the mountain, then lets you control your own speed through two full 360s on the way down.
adventure.bonus: Take your hands off the brake for one entire loop.

adventure.title: Boulder a Problem at Asana Climbing Gym
adventure.description: Garden City's bouldering-only gym is all movement and no ropes, with problems set for people who have never climbed and people who climb every day.
adventure.bonus: Top out one problem two grades above what you think you can do.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike Hulls Gulch from Camel's Back
adventure.description: Roll out of the North End straight onto the Ridge to Rivers network and climb foothill singletrack until the city disappears behind you.
adventure.bonus: Descend without touching your brakes on one full section.

adventure.title: Soak in the Pools at The Springs, Idaho City
adventure.description: An hour up the Ponderosa Pine byway, a proper hot springs resort with a big geothermal pool, a sauna and drinks brought to the water's edge.
adventure.bonus: Book an adults-only day and stay in the water until you have to be told to leave.

adventure.title: Run the Payette with Cascade Raft & Kayak
adventure.description: An hour north of town the Payette throws big, warm, forgiving whitewater, and Cascade has been guiding it out of Horseshoe Bend since 1985.
adventure.bonus: Volunteer for the front-left seat and take every wave to the face.

adventure.title: Float the Boise River from Barber Park
adventure.description: Rent a tube at Barber Park and drift six lazy miles of cold, clear river straight through the middle of the city to Ann Morrison Park.
adventure.bonus: Rope your whole group's tubes together and stay attached the entire float.

adventure.title: Paddleboard Quinn's Pond at Esther Simplot Park
adventure.description: Flat, warm water minutes from downtown with the foothills on the horizon and rental boards right at the shoreline.
adventure.bonus: Make it all the way across and back without falling in.

adventure.title: Soak at Kirkham Hot Springs Off Highway 21
adventure.description: Terraced granite pools sit right above the South Fork of the Payette with hot water running down the rock face like a shower.
adventure.bonus: Alternate a hot pool and a plunge in the cold river three times.

adventure.title: Drive to Redfish Lake and Stanley for the Day
adventure.description: Three hours up Highway 21 the Sawtooths rise straight out of an alpine lake, and Stanley is a 100-person town at the bottom of them.
adventure.bonus: Swim in Redfish Lake no matter what the water temperature is.

adventure.title: Ride the Boise River Greenbelt End to End
adventure.description: Twenty-five car-free miles of tree-shaded path trace the river past parks, breweries and the university with almost no reason to stop pedalling.
adventure.bonus: Finish at a patio you have never been to and order whatever the bartender is drinking.
